combination: dasatinib + quercetin (D+Q); quercetin is a supplement, included as adjunct only per plan section 0

approval.note: Approved BCR-ABL/SRC-family kinase inhibitor for Ph+ CML/ALL including pediatric use. Senolytic use is off-label.

claims.text: BubR1 insufficiency drives p16Ink4a-positive cellular senescence in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue; genetic p16Ink4a inactivation attenuates senescence and premature ageing in BubR1-insufficient mice.

In BubR1-hypomorphic progeroid mice, drug-inducible clearance of p16Ink4a-positive senescent cells delayed onset of age-related pathology in adipose tissue, skeletal muscle and eye, and attenuated established disease when started late in life - the direct causal evidence that senolysis modifies the BubR1-insufficiency phenotype.

Dasatinib + quercetin is the canonical senolytic pair: dasatinib clears senescent human fat-cell progenitors, quercetin clears senescent endothelial cells, and the combination reduced senescent-cell burden and extended healthspan in aged, irradiated and progeroid (Ercc1-/delta) mice.

First human evidence that D+Q lowers senescent-cell burden: in a 9-patient open-label diabetic-kidney-disease pilot, 3 days of D 100 mg + Q 1000 mg reduced adipose p16/p21-expressing cells, SA-beta-gal activity and circulating SASP factors (IL-1a, IL-6, MMP-9/12) within 11 days.

In a first-in-human open-label pilot in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (n=14), intermittent D+Q was feasible and improved physical-function measures; pulmonary function and reported health were unchanged - feasibility-level evidence, not efficacy proof.

MVA1 disease mechanism is chronic chromosome missegregation producing mosaic aneuploidy; aneuploid and damaged cells enter p53/p21- and p16-driven senescence, linking the BubR1 genotype to the senescent-cell burden that D+Q targets (MVA review; genotype-phenotype chain).

Counter-consideration: senescence is also a tumour-suppressive response, and aneuploid-cell proliferation is limited by a p53-dependent mechanism; indiscriminate removal of the senescent compartment in a cancer-predisposition syndrome could remove both harmful and protective arrested cells. Net direction in this genotype is untested.

pediatric.approved_pediatric_indication: Pediatric patients 1 year of age and older: Ph+ CML in chronic phase; newly diagnosed Ph+ ALL in combination with chemotherapy (quoted label fact).
pediatric.label_pediatric_dosing_fact: Label Table 1 starting dose by body weight, once daily (quoted label fact, not advice): 10-<20 kg 40 mg; 20-<30 kg 60 mg; 30-<45 kg 70 mg; >=45 kg 100 mg; tablets not recommended <10 kg.
key_risks: Label section 5.10 'Effects on Growth and Development in Pediatric Patients': epiphyses delayed fusion, osteopenia, growth retardation and gynecomastia reported; label advises monitoring bone growth and development. Directly relevant to a child with short stature and failure to thrive.
Myelosuppression (severe thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, anaemia) and bleeding; dasatinib also inhibits platelet function - additive bleeding risk with any antiplatelet adjunct.
Fluid retention incl. pleural effusions; pulmonary arterial hypertension; QT prolongation; severe dermatologic reactions; tumour lysis syndrome; embryo-fetal toxicity.

Hypothesis framing: senolytic regimens are intermittent 'hit-and-run' (3-day cycles in the human pilots), which limits total exposure relative to continuous oncology dosing - but no pediatric senolytic dosing exists; any use here is untested.
monitoring: Symptoms of fluid retention, PAH, QT interval
If ever used senolytically: p16/SA-beta-gal biomarker response before/after cycle (research setting only)

celegans.readout: embryonic/larval viability, him rate, growth rate, behavioural tracking
celegans.expected: dasatinib is an SRC-family inhibitor; C. elegans SRC ortholog src-1 exists - plausible senolytic-like clearance of damaged cells, but the worm lacks a classical senescent compartment; interpret cautiously

fibroblasts.assay: intermittent D+Q exposure of MVA patient fibroblasts
fibroblasts.readout: SA-beta-gal/p16+ cell fraction, SASP cytokines, aneuploidy rate by FISH/scDNA-seq, micronuclei
fibroblasts.expected: reduced senescent fraction and SASP; aneuploidy rate itself should be unchanged (senolytics do not repair the SAC)

scrnaseq.assay: signature reversal on patient scRNA-seq map

supplements.expected: quercetin itself sits in the supplement program, not as a drug candidate

verdict_reason: Strongest mechanistic-to-human chain of any candidate: the disease-relevant BubR1-hypomorph mouse is the literal model organism of the anchor senolysis study (PMID:22048312), and D+Q is the only candidate class with human evidence of senescent-cell clearance (PMID:31542391). Dasatinib is approved with a pediatric label; quercetin is adjunct-only per plan. Rank capped by the label's pediatric growth-retardation warning in a child whose phenotype includes short stature and failure to thrive, and by the untested risk of clearing a tumour-suppressive senescent compartment in a cancer-predisposition syndrome.
